pr_body:
In Elasticsearch we sometimes use geotile grid using arithmetic operations, for example calling GeoTileUtils#getXTile nd sometimes we resolve things geometrically by calling  GeoTileUtils#toBoundingBox. It is easy to prove that the geometric solution is equivalent to the arithmetic solution until zoom 19 using lucene encoding scheme for geo. After that, we can observe instabilities and solutions are not consistent.

In order to fix that we added some logic to GeoTileUtils#toBoundingBox that make sure the generated bounding boxes are consistent with the arithmetic solution and hence we can use both approaches indistintable, regardless the zoom level.

fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/92611
fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/95574
pr_title: Fix geo tile bounding boxes to be consistent with arithmetic method

review_comment: I've not been able to reason fully about this algorithm, but at first glance this predicate seems to be the opposite of what I'd expect.

You need to be aware that numbering for latitude goes from positive latitudes to negative latitudes.

 If we go up (steps are positive) we are already in the right tile and we want to find the point where the tile changes. When the next point is in a different tile, the current point is the one we are looking for. (this is the case if maths are good)

If we go down (steps are negative) then we are in the wrong tile so we need to find the point where it changes. That next point where it changes is the one we are looking for.

makes more sense?
